newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Telecom GSM talks drag on with US partners.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Telecom GSM talks drag on with US partners.

text.p: Slovak state telephone monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p. (ST) on Monday said protracted negotiations with U.S. partners over creating the country's second GSM mobile phone network were progressing, but more talks were needed.

"We will hold another round of talks on October 29-30 in the U.S., and we can say the negotiation already show certain signs of progress," Igor Huzevka, the ST consultant for the venture, told Reuters said without elaborating.
ST is negotiating with U.S. West Media Group Inc and Bell Atlantic Corp, its partners in an already functioning NMT analogue mobile phone network through a joint-venture Eurotel s.r.o.

In July the Eurotel owners agreed in principle to create a new company conforming to the government conditions. The crucial condition stipulates that the Slovak side must own at least 60 percent in the GSM operator.
ST holds 51 percent in Eurotel, with the two U.S. groups sharing the remaining 49 percent.
On September 4, the Ministry of Telecommunications formally granted one of the two planned GSM licences to Eurotel, under the contract for the NMT system signed in 1991.
The ministry said at the time that Eurotel owners had 90 days from signing the licence to officially create a joint-stock company to operate the system.

"All sides involved in the project believe that the final agreement will be reached before the ministry deadline," Huzevka said. "We are simply in the situation where the agreement has be to be reached, otherwise..." he did not finish the statement.

The ministry had warned that Eurotel could lose the GSM licence if its owners fail to meet the deadline, but also said such a development was not expected. Huzevka declined further comment on this possibility.

ST said the negotiations, dragging for over three months, are concentrated mainly on executive rights in the new company and the split of investments. It ruled out any changes to the composition of the group.
The second licence has been granted to Slovtel, a consortium of four Slovak energy companies, the state monopoly gas distributor and a private firm Hanco sro, which teamed up with France Telecom.
